title: ticket done --note must append the RESULT, not replace the GOAL

note:
GOAL: a card keeps both lines. ticket done --note must append its RESULT below the GOAL line already on the card, so a closed objective still says which outcome it served and what it achieved.

Found 25 Oct while closing o63: ticket done o63 --note "RESULT: ..." replaced the note written at claim time, and o63's GOAL line was gone from the card. The note is one string and done overwrites it, so every close silently loses the GOAL. Two options: append in the CLI, or refuse a done note that has no GOAL when the card already has one.

title: Machine-specific board keys: one repo from several boxes never clobbers another board

note:
GOAL: one repo used from several boxes keeps every machine's board intact. Each machine's key carries its own identity, so no board can clobber or shadow another; all machines' run files sit in the repo side by side and each machine reads only its own; the local state dir is a derived cache that can be rebuilt from the repo.

Source: Des's design direction, relayed by KLV KOR Guy, 25 Oct, straight after the origin-gate change. Context: the korolev sweep wiped live state mid-session and only the in-repo run survived; KLV rebuilt his board by hand from it.

Today the key is basename(realpath)-sha1(realpath)[0:8], a path hash with no machine in it, so two boxes mounting the repo at the same path produce the same key. Nothing about a run file in the repo says which machine wrote it.

Plan: machine identity (env override, then OS machine id, then hostname) in the state key; run files under history/<machine>/ with root-level files read as this machine's legacy; a state restore verb that rebuilds the state file from the repo and backs up what it replaces; docs say the state dir is a cache.

Open: which identity a containerised daemon should use, since a container hostname changes on recreate.
